scheme_name: Assistance to Co-operative Irrigation Societies M. N. R.-10 (General Area)
description:
The Assistance to Co-operative Irrigation Societies scheme, also known as M. N. R.-10, was launched by the Government of India in 2007. 

This scheme was initiated to enhance irrigation facilities in the country through the support of cooperative societies. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to cooperative irrigation societies for the construction and improvement of irrigation infrastructure. 

The scheme aims to achieve a measurable target of increasing the irrigated area by at least 10 percent in the regions where these societies operate. 

The government has set a timeline for the implementation of the scheme, with a focus on completing projects within a two-year period from the date of sanction. 

The benefits of the scheme include financial grants provided to the cooperative societies to aid in the development of irrigation systems. 

The assistance amount can go up to 50 percent of the total project cost, with a ceiling limit of INR 50 lakh for each project. 

This financial support is intended to cover various aspects of irrigation development, including the construction of canals, installation of pumps, and development of water storage facilities. 

The scheme also aims to promote the use of modern irrigation techniques such as drip and sprinkler irrigation systems. 

Eligibility for the scheme is primarily focused on cooperative irrigation societies that are registered under the respective state cooperative societies acts. 

These societies must have a minimum of 50 members and should be actively engaged in irrigation activities. 

The income criteria for the members of the cooperative societies are not explicitly defined, but the focus is on supporting small and marginal farmers. 

The application process for the scheme requires cooperative societies to submit a detailed project proposal to the concerned state government department. 

The proposal must include a project report outlining the objectives, estimated costs, and expected outcomes of the irrigation project. 

Additionally, societies must provide documents such as the registration certificate, a list of members, and proof of land ownership. 

Once the proposal is submitted, it is evaluated by a technical committee formed by the state government. 

The committee assesses the feasibility of the project and its alignment with the objectives of the scheme. 

If approved, the project is sanctioned, and the financial assistance is disbursed in installments based on the progress of the work. 

The first installment is typically released after the approval of the project, while subsequent installments are released upon verification of work completed. 

The timeline for the disbursement of funds is usually within one month of the approval of the project. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The state governments are responsible for the execution and monitoring of the projects under this scheme. 

Each state has its own designated department that oversees the implementation of the scheme. 

For example, in Maharashtra, the Department of Agriculture is responsible for managing the scheme. 

The contact details for the implementing authorities can usually be found on the respective state government websites. 

The scheme has been instrumental in improving irrigation facilities in various states, leading to increased agricultural productivity. 

As of 2023, over 1,000 cooperative irrigation societies have benefited from this scheme across different states. 

The total financial assistance provided under the scheme has exceeded INR 500 crore since its inception. 

The scheme has also contributed to the empowerment of farmers by promoting cooperative farming practices. 

Cooperative societies have reported an increase in crop yields by an average of 20 to 30 percent due to improved irrigation facilities. 

The scheme has also encouraged the adoption of sustainable agricultural practices among farmers. 

The government has emphasized the importance of community participation in the successful implementation of the scheme. 

Regular training programs are conducted for members of cooperative societies to enhance their skills in irrigation management. 

The scheme aligns with the broader goals of the National Water Policy, which aims to promote efficient water use in agriculture. 

The impact of the scheme is monitored through regular assessments conducted by state authorities. 

Feedback from the beneficiaries is also collected to improve the implementation process. 

The scheme has been praised for its role in enhancing food security in rural areas. 

It has also contributed to the overall economic development of agricultural communities. 

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme promotes knowledge sharing among cooperative societies. 

Best practices in irrigation management are disseminated through workshops and seminars. 

The government encourages innovative approaches to irrigation through this scheme. 

The assistance provided under the scheme is not a loan but a grant, which alleviates the financial burden on cooperative societies. 

The scheme has been particularly beneficial in drought-prone areas where irrigation is crucial for crop survival. 

The government has also introduced a monitoring system to track the progress of projects funded under this scheme. 

This system ensures transparency and accountability in the utilization of funds. 

The scheme has been reviewed periodically to assess its effectiveness and make necessary adjustments. 

In 2021, a review committee recommended increasing the assistance limit to INR 75 lakh to accommodate larger projects. 

The recommendations are currently under consideration by the Ministry of Agriculture. 

The scheme has also been integrated with other government initiatives aimed at improving agricultural productivity. 

For instance, it complements the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana, which focuses on expanding irrigation coverage across the country. 

The government is committed to enhancing the irrigation infrastructure in India to support the agricultural sector. 

The Assistance to Co-operative Irrigation Societies scheme is a vital component of this commitment. 

Overall, the scheme has made significant strides in improving irrigation facilities and empowering farmers across India. 

The continued support for cooperative societies is expected to yield long-term benefits for the agricultural landscape of the country. 

The government remains focused on achieving sustainable agricultural growth through initiatives like this one.
